# Radiators Radiators are devices that exchange thermal energy between a [textlink="pipenet" link="PipeNetworks"] and the surrounding environment.
Radiators are completely passive and require no power. They always try to equalize the temperature of the gas in the [textlink="pipenet" link="PipeNetworks"] with the surrounding environment.
Radiators transfer heat in two ways: convection and radiation. - Convection transfers heat through the movement of gas. - Radiation transfers heat through electromagnetic waves.
If a radiator is in a vacuum, it can only transfer heat through radiation. If it is surrounded by an atmosphere, it can transfer heat through both convection and radiation.
Through convection, you can only cool or heat the gas to the temperature of the atmosphere or [textlink="pipenet" link="PipeNetworks"] with which it is exchanging heat, provided that the temperature of the gas in the [textlink="pipenet" link="PipeNetworks"] or atmosphere remains constant.
If you are exchanging heat with space, you can only cool the gas to the temperature of space. To increase the efficiency of radiation, build radiators over a grille: a radiator will radiate more heat there than when mounted directly on plating.
Gas naturally flows through a radiator due to pressure differences, but a gas pump can be used to increase the flow rate.
Increasing the flow of gas through a radiator increases the rate of heat exchange.
